PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

minutes_text:
AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Assistant City Manager Domic led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Councilmember Argumedo offered the invocation. 

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. City Videos Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk Lena Shumway, along with IT Specialist Kevin Torres, provided an overview of the MyCommerce app for the City of Commerce.

The discussion included the rollout plan and strategies to ensure residents are well-informed about the application. Recommendations were made to create an instructional video explaining the app’s features and functionality, as well as to host training sessions at the Library and Senior Center. 

It was also suggested to update the app’s backdrop for a more modern appearance. Additional discussions focused on the established response timeframes, ensuring service requests are addressed promptly, and clarifying who will be responsible for monitoring the app’s implementation.

PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individual wishing to address the City Council on any items within their jurisdiction.  




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo

5.. Appointment of Candidates to fill two (2) Executive Management Vacancies

4.. Approving Blanket Authority to File Applications for Grant Funds from the Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District for Measure A Funding for Projects and Programs

2.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 13A, 13B and 13C

3.. Approval of Minutes

SCHEDULED MATTERS

6.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Jimenez provided a recap of activities and incidents for the month of January.

Councilmember Rebollo commended the efforts made to assist residents affected by the fires.

Councilmember Argumedo expressed his gratitude to everyone who responded to the fires and requested a follow-up on addressing graffiti issues in the Bandini area.

7.. Authorize Submittal of Calhome Application to the California Department of Housing and Community Development and Related Supporting Actions  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo City Manager Hernandez provided an overview of the staff report.

Councilmember Rebollo praised the program, highlighting that residents could apply for up to $200,000 in assistance. Further discussion took place regarding the CDBG Rehabilitation Program and how both programs could complement each other while ensuring the existing CDBG program remains operational. It was also noted that this program allows for interior repairs. City Manager Hernandez mentioned the possibility of lowering the maximum application amount to make funding accessible to more residents.

Mayor Pro Tem Lainez emphasized that there is no cost to the City to apply for the program; however, administrative and application service fees will apply once funding is received.

8.. Committee and Commission Appointments Mayor Altamirano appointed Brandi Alvarez to the Library Commission. 

PUBLIC HEARING

9.. Participation in the Los Angeles Urban County Permanent Local Housing Allocation Program and Approval of a Reimbursable Contract with Los Angeles County Development Authority  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Acting Director of Economic Development and Planning Morales and Adriana Robledo with Avant Garde, provided an overview of the staff report.

During the discussion, questions were raised about whether this funding is separate from CDBG funding and whether only owner-occupied residences would be eligible for the program. Ms. Robledo stated that she would review whether rental units and ADUs could be included. City Manager Hernandez clarified that as long as the owner resides in one of the units, they would qualify for the program.

Mayor Altamirano opened the public hearing. As no individuals wished to address the City Council on this item, Mayor Altamirano closed the public hearing.




CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Rebollo congratulated all employees recognized at the Employee Service Awards event and praised the Saturday Commissioner Breakfast as a wonderful event. She also requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory of River Tobias Fawl.

Councilmember Garcia reported attending both the Employee Service Awards and the Commissioner Appreciation Breakfast. She congratulated the Parks and Recreation Department on the success of the water aerobics class and suggested including in the budget additional aerobics and swim lessons for summer. Additionally, she thanked the City Manager for providing updates on Veterans Park.

Councilmember Rebollo also extended her appreciation to the Parks and Recreation staff and the Commission on Disabilities and Opportunities for bringing the Special Olympics to Commerce.

Mayor Pro Tem Lainez attended the Metro meeting at the Senior Center regarding the Eastside Transit Corridor Project. He noted that questions were raised about funding and the project's progress, emphasizing that while the funding outlook remains uncertain, efforts must continue to move the project forward. He also congratulated the employees recognized at the Employee Service Awards and expressed his appreciation for the Commissioner Appreciation Breakfast.

Mayor Altamirano reported attending both the Service Recognition event and the Commissioner Appreciation Breakfast. He provided an update on the In-N-Out project, stating that despite some delays, it is expected to move forward and is anticipated to open in May 2026.


ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:14 pm in memory of River Tobias Fowl.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
